source.title: Position-aware Automatic Circuit Discovery
source.authors: Tal Haklay; Hadas Orgad; David Bau; Aaron Mueller; Yonatan Belinkov

record.tranche_reason: The study uses position-aware edge attribution and circuit faithfulness evaluation, rather than the original study’s head-specific circuit analysis, to examine IOI circuit faithfulness and how it varies with circuit construction and evaluation settings.
record.gate_note: IOI faithfulness curves compare position-aware schema circuits with non-positional circuits and compare schema variants. Plotted values are not numerically stated in the text, so they are recorded as figure only. The paper reports IOI prediction accuracy in Table 2, but those rates are used to define eligible examples and do not test the claimed mechanism. It does not identify or test the original 26 heads or their roles.
record.test_reason: A circuit-discovery methods paper (PEAP plus schemas). IOI serves only as a benchmark: every IOI result compares the faithfulness of the authors' own position-aware circuits (human, LLM, LLM+mask schemas) with a non-positional EAP baseline. It never examines the Wang et al. circuit, its heads or roles, backup heads, or circuit overlap. It also does not vary ablation type or metric on the original circuit. The hard/soft faithfulness curves measure the authors' method, not the sensitivity of the IOI circuit's evaluation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that position-aware edge attribution with dataset schemas gives better circuit size-faithfulness trade-offs than position-agnostic discovery. They find that LLM-generated schemas, especially with saliency masks, match or slightly exceed human-designed schemas. They also argue that schemas should be tailored to the model-task pair, citing Llama-3-8B IOI.
record.recipe_differences: Uses position-aware edge attribution patching and schema-level circuit construction, then evaluates faithfulness by ablating edges outside the circuit. It does not reproduce the original head-specific circuit analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Faithfulness is evaluated across circuit size and varies with positional versus non-positional construction and schema choice. The paper compares hard and soft faithfulness; it reports no significant hard-faithfulness differences across GPT2-small IOI prompt orders or pipeline trials.

fits_no_version.finding: On IOI in GPT2-small, EAP edge rankings change substantially when scores are aggregated across positions. Top-1% set difference is 17.1% for cancellation and 17.5% for overestimation, against roughly 3.9% and 3.6% in controls (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automatic edge-attribution circuit discovery on IOI is sensitive to how scores are aggregated across token positions.

fits_no_version.finding: Position-aware circuits reach high hard faithfulness on IOI with far fewer edges than non-positional circuits, in GPT2-small and Llama-3-8B (Fig. 6, 9, 10; figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The size-faithfulness trade-off of automatically discovered IOI circuits improves when token position is distinguished.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2025)
record.problems: IOI circuits are evaluated only on examples where each model can predict the correct answer. Faithfulness curves are mostly figure-only, with no numerical values or uncertainty estimates stated for the IOI comparisons. The study does not test the original head classes, their roles, or circuit overlap with the original circuit.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. IOI accuracy rates in Table 2 are described in gate_note because they define eligible examples and do not test the circuit mechanism.

untested.parts: Original 26 heads, 7 classes, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria are not examined.
No name-mover ablation or backup-head analysis.
Circuits are found in Llama-3-8B, but head classes and roles are not compared with GPT-2 small; no component reuse.
No overlap with the original circuit; no comparison of ablation types.
No variation of ablation, metric or prompt distribution applied to the original circuit; no claim about how much of IOI the circuit explains.
No test of shared components across name orders or templates. ABBA and BABA circuits are built separately.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and V5 'supports' labels are not justified: all IOI rows compare the authors' method variants with a baseline. IOI datasets are filtered to correctly answered examples (GPT2-small ABBA 92.5%, Llama-3-8B ABBA 71.7%). The human IOI schema extends the Wang et al. positions (IO, S1, S1+1, S2, END), but this is a design input, not a test.

versions.untested_parts: The paper discovers and evaluates its own circuits; it does not test whether the original GPT-2 small 26-head, 7-class circuit or its stated head roles and faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria hold.
No main name-mover ablation or backup-head self-repair test.
It evaluates IOI circuits in GPT2-small and Llama-3-8B, but does not compare whether the same head classes and roles are present across models, checkpoints, or tasks, or test component reuse.

It compares positional and non-positional circuit faithfulness, but does not measure circuit overlap or establish that other methods recover essentially the same circuit; it does not compare ablation types.

Tests positionality/schema choices and hard/soft faithfulness on IOI, including prompt-order and trial comparisons. Does not test alternative ablation types on the original circuit, and does not establish that the original circuit explains only part of IOI behavior.
It evaluates separately discovered circuits on IOI prompt orders, but does not test whether the same components or mechanism carry IOI across orders, templates, or more names.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: IOI-ABBA circuit-size sweeps on GPT2-small and Llama-3-8B
reader_labels.reason: Faithfulness trade-offs differ between position-aware schema circuits and non-positional circuits; the reported position-aware advantage and schema-method comparisons support evaluation sensitivity in these settings (r1-r8, r9-r16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT2-small hard faithfulness across IOI prompt orders and pipeline trials
